whatItFakes: A holder whose party the roster doesn't record (a statewide executive such as an attorney general or treasurer, or a legislative seat with no roster row) sits in the party that carried the state in 2024; a lieutenant governor on the governor's ticket takes the governor's party.
why: The offices research records each statewide office's term and vacancy rule but not its holder's party, and the legislative roster has no row for a few seats.
replacement: Each statewide executive's real party from a public roster (Ballotpedia's partisan composition of state executive offices, or each state's own election results). Oct 23, 2026 (research-gov-sourced-parameters): unrecordedParty in src/core2/modules/officials.ts now reads data/research/offices/unrecorded-holder-parties-2026.json first: the five territory governors (National Governors Association), the American Samoa and Northern Marianas lieutenant governors and attorney general (Wikipedia), ten offices elected without party labels, whose holders sit with no party (Wikipedia, Ballotpedia), the Guam, Virgin Islands, Northern Marianas and American Samoa legislatures (Wikipedia party counts, assigned to their at-large seats in order), and 42 state legislative seats the Open States roster leaves vacant (Ballotpedia's 2025 and 2026 vacancy tables: the departing member's party). Still estimated (the file's unreadSeats): six vacant seats with no Ballotpedia vacancy row, the Virgin Islands boards of education and of elections, and the seats the game creates when a Census district name does not match the roster's (gov-offices-roster-district-name-mismatch, which removes them).
